facts.value: Overtraining occurs when a person exceeds their body's ability to recover from strenuous exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Overtraining can be described as a point at which a person may have a decrease in performance or plateau as a result of failure to perform at a certain level or training-load consistently; a load which exceeds their recovery capacity.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: People who are overtrained cease making progress, and can even begin to lose strength and fitness.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Overtraining is also known as chronic fatigue, burnout, and overstress in athletes.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Monotonous program overtraining suggests that repetition of the same movement can cause performance plateau due to an adaption of the central nervous system, resulting from a lack of stimulation.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Chronic overwork-type overtraining occurs when training with too high intensity or volume without allowing sufficient recovery time.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Up to 10% of elite endurance athletes and 10% of American college swimmers are affected by overtraining syndrome.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Overtraining syndrome is characterized by unexplained underperformance for approximately 2 weeks, even after having adequate resting time.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc
